title: Godot editor's automatic display scaling gets weird in multi-monitor setups
body: ### Tested versions Godot 4.5.1 stable ### System information Gentoo, X11, Cinnamon ### Issue description I have a unique multi-monitor setup with two 3440x1440 monitors and two 1080p monitors. It looks like this: I opened Godot, created a project, parked the editor window in the right half of display 3 (green), closed Godot, opened Godot again. The project selection window (which appeared in the middle of display 3 (green)) had normal scale, but when I opened the project, the editor window location was restored to the right side of display 3 (green) but the UI scale was like 4x bigger than before and the editor window lacked the maximize button in top right corner. This was solved by moving the editor window to the center of screen 4 (light blue) and restarting Godot. I then disabled automatic display scaling in editor settings and the problem went away permanently. I think the issue is that the display auto-scaling feature tries to get the display scale from the nearest monitor, but the middle of the window is closer to the middle of the low-resolution 1080p display (yellow) than it is to the middle of the high-resolution display (green) that it is actually fully contained in. Maybe a better algorithm would be determining which display the window midpoint is located on and if it's off-screen, then falling back to the nearest display. Anyway, this is an ultra-low-priority bug. Just thought I'd let you know. ### Steps to reproduce Difficult to reproduce without having multiple monitors of different sizes, but the basic steps are in the issue description. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) This issue is not project-related.
